events.title: King Duncan I of Scotland is killed by Macbeth
events.description: Duncan I was killed in battle near Elgin by Macbeth, who took the throne. Macbeth ruled for 17 years, a far more capable king than the villain of Shakespeare's play written five centuries later.
events.html: Duncan I was killed in battle near Elgin by Macbeth, who took the throne. Macbeth ruled for 17 years, a far more capable king than the villain of Shakespeare's play written five centuries later.

events.title: The Mainz Psalter becomes the first dated printed book
events.description: Johann Fust and Peter Schöffer completed the Mainz Psalter, the first printed book to carry a date and printer's names. It also pioneered colour printing with its red and blue initials.
events.html: Johann Fust and Peter Schöffer completed the Mainz Psalter, the first printed book to carry a date and printer's names. It also pioneered colour printing with its red and blue initials.

events.title: International forces relieve the besieged legations in Beijing
events.description: Troops of the Eight-Nation Alliance entered Beijing and lifted the 55-day siege of the foreign legations by Boxers and Qing troops. China was forced to pay a crushing indemnity.
events.html: Troops of the Eight-Nation Alliance entered Beijing and lifted the 55-day siege of the foreign legations by Boxers and Qing troops. China was forced to pay a crushing indemnity.

events.title: Franklin Roosevelt signs the Social Security Act
events.description: Roosevelt signed the Social Security Act, creating old-age pensions, unemployment insurance and aid for dependent children. It became the cornerstone of the American welfare state.
events.html: Roosevelt signed the Social Security Act, creating old-age pensions, unemployment insurance and aid for dependent children. It became the cornerstone of the American welfare state.

events.title: Japan accepts the Allied terms of surrender
events.description: Japan's government notified the Allies that it accepted the Potsdam Declaration, and President Truman announced the news that evening. Emperor Hirohito recorded a broadcast to his people for the next day.
